headline: Twelve distinct class strings across a thousand buttons is the shape a build-time compiler resolves completely: `@yak/solid` picks the class at compile time and leads at 2.71M renders/s with no library code left at runtime.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

microbench.why: The conditional interpolations resolve to a fixed set of classes, so both yak compilers can decide the class list without running anything: `yak-solid` books zero lib self-time and leads at 2.71M renders/s, `next-yak` books 0.294 ms and reaches 1.68M. `next-yak-nofold` at 721,000 shows what the same source costs when the wrapper stays, less than half the folded lane. The cached mergers do well here as the case predicts — `cnfast` at 1.60M and `cn` at 1.49M, since twelve repeated strings make almost every lookup a hit — while `styled-components` at 536,000 and `emotion` at 321,000 rebuild the class string per instance even though only twelve exist.

autocannon.why: `yak-solid` answers 1,750 req/s and `next-yak` 1,490, with `next-yak-css` also at 1,490. `cnfast` holds 1,040 and `cn` 929; `panda-props` at 370 resolves style props per instance inside the request.

attribution.why: `yak-solid` renders in 0.425 ms with nothing in the lib bucket at all. `next-yak` at 0.618 ms splits 0.324 ms of react-dom against 0.294 ms of yak, and `next-yak-css` at 0.697 ms carries an empty lib bucket because a static css prop compiles to a plain class. `emotion` needs 3.08 ms with 1.94 ms inside its own runtime.

hydrate.why: `yak-solid` at 30.2 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 32.9 ms claim the markup without building a tree; the React lanes start at 43.7 ms. `goober` at 130 ms and `emotion` at 116 ms pay their first style injection during hydration.

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 4.1 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 5.1 ms lead the React field's ~7.5 ms, though React writes nothing on this pass while the Solid lanes re-evaluate the variant and swap the class. `emotion` at 12.9 ms is the only lane that separates on mechanism rather than framework.

mount.why: `yak-solid` mounts in 20.0 ms and `vanilla-solid` in 21.4 ms, against 70.5 ms for `next-yak` and 102 ms for `emotion`. With the class decided at build time the cold mount is template cloning; the runtime lanes inject their sheet before the first paint.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, near 0.13 ms. Twelve class strings across a thousand elements is a cache hit for the style engine no matter which lane produced them.

payload.why: The next-yak css-prop lanes are the lightest at roughly 3,730 gz B, with `vanilla` at 3,789 B. `yak-solid` reaches 9,309 B, its markup carrying a hydration key per element. The utility lanes are the heavy end — `cn` 17,553 B, `cnfast` 16,093 B, `tailwind-merge` 15,130 B — where the whole difference is library JS for a page whose CSS is 226 B.

nsweep.why: `yak-solid` holds 1.15 ms at 4,000 instances and `next-yak` 1.94 ms, both flat, because a decided class has no per-instance work to scale. `panda-props` at 8.17 ms and `emotion` at 11.3 ms grow with every element.
